answer_text:
Let \(X\) be the fish weight in grams. We are given

\[
X \sim N(a=375,\ \sigma=25).
\]

Standardize using

\[
Z=\frac{X-375}{25},
\]

where \(Z \sim N(0,1)\). Let \(\Phi(z)\) denote the standard normal CDF.

---

### a) Probability the weight is from 300 g to 425 g

\[
P(300 \le X \le 425)
= P\left(\frac{300-375}{25} \le Z \le \frac{425-375}{25}\right)
\]

\[
= P(-3 \le Z \le 2)
\]

\[
= \Phi(2)-\Phi(-3)
\]

Using standard normal table values,

\[
\Phi(2) \approx 0.9772,
\qquad
\Phi(-3)=1-\Phi(3)\approx 1-0.99865=0.00135.
\]

Thus,

\[
P(300 \le X \le 425)
\approx 0.9772-0.00135
= 0.9759.
\]

---

### b) Probability the weight is no more than 450 g

\[
P(X \le 450)
= P\left(Z \le \frac{450-375}{25}\right)
= P(Z \le 3)
\]

\[
= \Phi(3)
\approx 0.99865.
\]

So,

\[
P(X \le 450) \approx 0.9987.
\]

---

### c) Probability the weight is more than 300 g

\[
P(X > 300)
= P\left(Z > \frac{300-375}{25}\right)
= P(Z > -3)
\]

\[
= 1-\Phi(-3)
= \Phi(3)
\approx 0.99865.
\]

So,

\[
P(X > 300) \approx 0.9987.
\]

---

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\text{a) } P(300 \le X \le 425) &\approx 0.9759,\\
\text{b) } P(X \le 450) &\approx 0.9987,\\
\text{c) } P(X > 300) &\approx 0.9987.
\end{aligned}
}
\]
